description: One row per (adm2_ucode, hazard_code). Columns follow the ' Data Schema' sheet of Global Hazard Data catalog.xlsx. Computed by the GEE exposure pipeline (CSV release 2026-08-31); for some hazards (heatwave, extreme heat, ASI, malaria) GEE used a different version of the layer than the hazard COGs in this catalog, so the numbers can differ from a recomputation on the COGs. Join to adm2 on adm2_ucode = ucode.

table:columns.name: hazs_mean
table:columns.description: Average intensity value of the hazard across the assessed administrative area. Higher numbers mean the physical danger is generally greater.

table:columns.name: hazs_std
table:columns.description: How much the intensity varies within the assessed administrative area. A large value means some locations are much riskier than others.

table:columns.name: hazs_max
table:columns.description: Highest hazard intensity within the administrative area. Higher values indicate severe localized impacts.

table:columns.name: hazs_min
table:columns.description: Lowest hazard intensity within the administrative area. Lower values represent minimal hazard intensity.

table:columns.name: hazs_median
table:columns.description: Middle value of hazard intensity when ranked from lowest to highest within the administrative area. Higher median refers to moderate–high intensity.

table:columns.name: gindex
table:columns.description: A 0–10 index scaled using global minimum and maximum hazard intensity values. Higher values indicate more severe global hazard levels.

table:columns.name: cindex
table:columns.description: A 0–10 index scaled using country-specific minimum and maximum hazard intensity values. Higher values indicate severe national-level hazard conditions.

table:columns.name: rindex
table:columns.description: A 0–10 index scaled using regional intensity extremes. Higher values reflect more severe regional hazard conditions.
